options.text: What's the word on the iron-line men?
Is it true the trench army attacks in waves until your arms give out?
How many soldiers can the diggers actually put in the field?
Do the men in the mud ever break and run?
I keep hearing about a 'quota' in the trenches across the way. Know anything?
They say the cold itself fights for the trench folk. True?
Do you respect the diggers? Even a little?
If the trench army has a weakness, what would it be?
Who commands those wave assaults?
Would your side ever strike a bargain with the shovel men?
I passed their earthworks yesterday. They're spreading.
Their singing carries across the valley after dark. Ever heard it?
Rumor says the mud soldiers lost a whole company last week.
Are your own soldiers scared of the men in the trenches?
What do the trench men do with their prisoners, do you know?
Why hasn't anyone pushed the diggers off this front yet?
Is it true the trench army eats the same grey soup every single day?
Any news of the precision army?
Are the drill-perfect types as untouchable as they claim?
They say the disciplined ones can speak across miles in moments. How?
Their supply columns run like clockwork, I'm told.
Do the parade-ground soldiers ever crack?
Be honest — is their discipline something you envy?
Where does the clockwork army rust?
Who writes all their precious orders?
Could your people ever sit at a table with the shield-bearers?
I watched them drill this morning. Not one step out of place.
Word is they keep a ledger of every favor and every slight.
Do the by-the-book soldiers fight after dark, or is that off the schedule?
I heard one of their patrols never made it home.
Does the steel-and-drill crowd worry your side?
How do the rulebook soldiers treat their captives?
Their watchtowers keep multiplying. Have you noticed?
Do the precise ones really pay their soldiers in written credit?
What do you make of the desert fighters?
Do the desert people really vanish at night?
How many of the dune folk are there, truly?
They say whoever drinks from a marked well owes the sand people a debt.
Your sentries whisper about shadows walking the wire. The dune folk?
Any grudging respect for the ambushers? At all?
The mirage folk must have a soft spot somewhere.
Does anyone actually lead the desert bands?
Would your side ever bargain with the dune raiders?
I crossed the dunes and saw nothing at all. Somehow that worried me more.
People claim sandstorms follow their war parties.
Is it true no one has ever caught one of the sand people sleeping?
Someone told me the desert bands took losses at the ridge.
Do your soldiers fear the quiet ones?
What happens to soldiers the sand people carry off?
Couldn't you just starve them out by seizing the wells?
I heard even their ambushes wait politely until the tea is finished.
Any news from the front?
Where's the worst of the fighting right now?
I heard steel ringing beyond the hill this morning. What happened?
Has anyone raided lately?
What happened at the ridge? Everyone keeps whispering about it.
Was last week's clash as bloody as they say?
It's been quiet lately. Does that worry you?
Where do you reckon the fighting moves next?
Somebody said a border post changed hands. True?
You look like you've just come from a fight. What happened?
I passed wounded men on the road. Whose were they?
There was smoke on the horizon at dawn. Yours, or theirs?
The traders on the road are spooked. What have they seen?
Is this fighting season or waiting season?
How are supplies holding up on this front?
I hear rations are short everywhere. Here too?
What's scarce enough right now to fetch a good price?
What would a trader do well to bring to this front?
Did a supply convoy really go missing last week?
Is any of the three sides actually going hungry?
Word is iron's getting hard to come by.
They say timber for the walls is running out.
Is anyone short of clean water?
Is there a quiet trade running between the lines? Smugglers?
Do the other quartermasters pay better than yours do?
Will the stores last through the cold season?
The old folk say the weather carries omens. Do you believe it?
That red sky last evening — do soldiers read anything into it?
The birds all went silent yesterday. Did your sentries notice?
There's a storm building. Good sign or bad?
Full moon coming. Does that change anything out here?
Do your soldiers carry charms? Believe in luck?
Three sentries, the same nightmare, the same night. Heard that one?
This fog rolled in strangely fast. Natural, you think?
What's the worst omen a soldier can see before a battle?
People say the land itself knows when a battle is coming.
Who moves out there after dark?
I saw lights crossing the valley last night. Whose were they?
Do the raids mostly come at night?
What do the night sentries talk about?
Someone told me you can hear digging under the ground at night.
It's dark and you're wide awake. Expecting something?
Those colored flashes on the ridgeline after sunset — signals?
What's that sound the wind carries after midnight?
Is it true attacks come at dawn more than any other hour?
Could someone slip between the lines in the dark?
I counted more campfires than usual across the valley.
Is there an hour when even soldiers won't step beyond the wire?
So who's actually winning this war?
If it all ended today, who'd hold the most ground?
Honestly — what are your side's chances?
Which of the three sides can last the longest?
Do soldiers bet on how this all ends?
Looks like a stalemate from where I'm standing.
Was there ever a moment the war turned, one way or another?
Travelers say no side can win this thing. Are they wrong?
Could someone from outside tip the balance?
Give me a year. When does it end?
How will the histories tell this war, do you think?
Whoever wins — will any of it have been worth it?
A deserter in a tavern told me all three camps are on their last legs.
What do people out here say about me?
Go on, say it. What do your people call me?
Am I watched when I travel these roads?
I've crossed blades with your people. Does the camp talk about it?
Is there a way back once a name goes bad with your side?
Any wild stories going around about me?
Is there a price on my head anywhere?
Do the other camps ever ask about me?
I've tried to deal fairly out here. Does anyone notice?
What did your side make of me when I first turned up?
You lot gossip like fishwives. Is any of it ever true?
Enough gossip. I'm off.
I'll keep my ears open elsewhere.
The road's calling. Keep the rumors warm for me.
Forget I asked. Take care.

negative: Asking us about us. Testing the echo? Move on.
The line describes itself in person. Wait around.
neutral: What's said about us? That we're endless. Half true. The other half is also endless.
We're the ones still here. That is the entire rumor and the entire truth.
positive: They say we're made of mud and stubbornness, friend. Flattery. There's also soup.
Rumors about the line come and go. The line stays. Draw your conclusion.

negative: Intel on Vostok? From you? Amusing. Half our Vostok files mention you.
You'd enjoy our assessment of the trench army. Flagged individuals get no assessments.
Ask them yourself. You seem practiced at making their acquaintance.
neutral: Assessment: unlimited patience, limited imagination. They absorb losses that would break a doctrine-led force.
Their wave assaults are predictable to the minute. Stopping them anyway costs more than the prediction is worth.
We track their quota cycles. When their command needs numbers, the front gets loud. It's due soon.
positive: Off the record, friend: their entrenching speed is genuinely impressive. We timed it. Then we doubled our estimate.
Between us, Vostok's weakness is roads. Their whole mass moves at soup-wagon speed. File that away.
One of their sergeants held a flooded trench six days straight. It's cited in our own training file. Don't repeat that.

negative: You ask about the iron line with their blood still drying on your name. Bold nose, short whiskers.
The diggers can speak for themselves. To you, they mostly have, I hear.
Why share our reading of the trench men with someone the wind distrusts?
neutral: The trench people are a flood — slow, loud, and honest about where it's going. One respects a flood. From a dune.
They dig, they hold, they endure. Sand does the same, and asks no rations. We prefer our method.
Their strength is that they do not tire of dying. Their weakness is the same sentence.
positive: Truth over tea, friend: of the two armies, the diggers frighten us more. Precision sleeps at night. Stubbornness doesn't.
Their columns cannot cross the deep sand — too heavy, too thirsty. So we sleep well. Mostly.
One winter they fed a stranded caravan of ours rather than seize it. We remember. It will not blunt our blades. But we remember.

negative: The clipboard army? Ask someone who owes you an answer. We count what you owe first.
Our thoughts on the polished ones are for allies. You are inventory.
Why would we brief you on anyone? You're on our slate already.
neutral: The polished ones fight like clockmakers. Beautiful. Clocks stop when you apply enough hammer.
Their patrols run to the minute. Convenient. We set our watches by their mistakes.
They log everything. Somewhere there's a form for being overrun. We intend to see it filed.
positive: Between us, friend, their signal towers are the real weapon. Blades we match. The talking-at-distance we envy.
Their supply columns are fat and punctual. The line drools a little. Don't tell them.
Give the polished ones this: they collect their wounded under fire, every time. Even we nod at that.

negative: Fishing for our own file. That's a new approach. Denied.
Curious what we say about ourselves? The recruitment poster is public. Start there.
neutral: What's said about us tends to be accurate. We issue corrections otherwise.
The claims about us are audited. Untouchable, no. Prepared, yes.
positive: The rumor I like best says we plan our victories a season ahead. We let that one circulate.
They say our sentries never sleep. False. They sleep on schedule, friend.

negative: The shield-men keep a thick file on you, I hear. Perhaps ask what they say about you instead.
You want gossip about the orderly ones? Buy it with trust. Yours is counterfeit here.
The wind does not discuss one hunter with another. Especially one so bloodied.
neutral: The orderly ones fear one thing: surprise. So we serve it seasonally, like fruit.
Their walls are strong, their schedules stronger. A schedule is a map of where a man will be. Think on that.
Untouchable, they claim. The desert has touched them twice this year. Quietly. They logged it as weather.
positive: Their discipline is real, friend. Break one plan and they simply unfold another. Like fighting a patient river.
We admire their water discipline, of all things. An army that rations well plans to live. Watch them.
A secret for the tea you shared: their far posts change watch at the same hour everywhere. Uniformity is a lovely gift.

negative: The sand people? Worry about the people in front of you. We're closer and you're owing.
We don't trade words about the dune folk with someone whose count is red.
Ask the desert yourself. You're halfway to being buried in it as far as we're concerned.
neutral: The dune folk fight like mosquitoes. Laugh if you want. Mosquitoes empty a man eventually.
They vanish at night, yes. So does our patience. One morning the line will be standing on their wells.
You can't dig a trench against smoke. So we dig deeper and post more eyes. Expensive smoke, that lot.
positive: Honest talk, friend: the desert ones spooked our recruits so badly we now drill against 'noises'. An entire drill. Noises.
Their trick is thirst — they let the desert besiege you for them. Respect from us, and we respect almost nothing.
One of ours wandered the flats three days. Woke with a full waterskin and a warning knotted in his laces. Make of that what you will.

negative: Intelligence on the desert bands is compartmentalized. Your compartment is 'outside'.
The ambushers' file stays shut for you. Half its recent pages involve people like you anyway.
You ask about ghosts while trailing your own. Settle your ledger first.
neutral: Threat assessment: small numbers, outsized effect. They attack schedules, not soldiers. It works more than we report.
They do vanish at night. Heat discipline, terrain memory, and nerve. We can model two of the three.
Every convoy through the dry sector budgets a loss percentage. That percentage has a name, and it's theirs.
positive: Candidly, friend: our doctrine struggles with them. You cannot combine arms against an enemy who declines to be found.
Their well markings are a functioning law code. We honor them on patrol. Command never wrote it down, but we all do it.
A desert guide once walked our lost patrol to water and vanished before thanks. The debt is logged. Aegis pays its ledgers.

negative: You ask the mirage about the mirage. Enjoy the answer you get.
What are we? The last thing several curious people wondered.
neutral: The stories about us are wrong in useful ways. We leave them uncorrected.
Do we vanish at night? The night is big and we are polite guests in it.
positive: Most rumors about us we started ourselves, friend. The frightening ones are the cheapest sentries we own.
They say we are ghosts. Ghosts need no water. We are thirstier and more patient than any ghost.

negative: Front news travels to friends. You're a different column in the book.
The recent fighting? You'll get the tour, not the telling, if you linger.
neutral: Steel at the ridge two nights back. Their push, our mud, the usual score: nobody happy, everybody digging.
A border post changed hands twice this week. By now it's mostly splinters with a flag.
positive: You missed a loud one, friend. Their line came singing confidence and left carrying quiet. The mud keeps the details.
News? Third company found a cellar of preserves in the ruins. Strategically, nothing. For morale, a historic victory.

negative: Operational updates are for cleared personnel. You are the opposite of cleared.
Recent contacts are under review. Your interest in them is itself under review.
neutral: Two skirmishes this week, both probing actions, both repelled. Pattern suggests a larger push is being priced.
The smoke you saw was a supply cache denied to the enemy. Controlled burn. Mostly controlled.
positive: Situation for your ears, friend: the eastern approach went quiet, which we distrust. Move west if you value calm.
Last night's flare-up was ours — a probe met early and turned around. Textbook. I get to say that maybe twice a year.

negative: News of battles finds friends first, strangers late, and enemies mid-battle. Guess your delivery time.
The fighting is wherever you keep walking without asking. Shall I not spoil it?
neutral: Blades spoke at the dry ford, briefly. The river now has opinions about both armies.
There was a raid; there was a reply; the vultures adjudicated. The verdict favored no banner.
positive: For your ears at this fire, friend: the two heavy armies mauled each other by the ridge, and we watched. Almost peaceful.
The road you came by hosted an ambush at dusk yesterday. Not ours. Sloppy work. You have luck — spend it slowly.

negative: Our stores are counted by people who count strangers too. Walk on.
Shortages? Ask your own pockets how they got so full.
neutral: Rations are thin, boots thinner, complaints plentiful. So, a normal year.
Iron comes slow lately. The forges upline blame the roads. The roads blame the war. The war says nothing.
positive: Friend, bring salt or thread next visit and the cooks will make you a legend. Coin is paper here; salt is government.
The convoy that vanished last week? Found. Driver drunk in a hayloft, cargo intact. Best news of the month, honestly.

negative: Logistics questions from outside the chain read as targeting data. This exchange is over.
Supply status is classified above your existence.
neutral: Supply holds at acceptable margins. The margin's exact width stays our business.
Scarce right now: lamp oil, bandage linen, patience. Trade the first two well and you'll do fine.
positive: Vendor tip, friend: bring timber and canvas to any of our posts and the quartermasters will outbid each other. Not a rumor.
Between us, the cold season stores are already secured. Someone upstream did their sums beautifully. Sleep easy.

negative: Our hunger and our plenty are twins we introduce to no one.
You ask what we lack. Company we trust. The shortage stands.
neutral: The desert's stores are the desert's secret. Traders find our terms fair and our inventories invisible.
Water is measured, dates are counted, and both outlast every siege so far attempted.
positive: Bring cloth dyes and honest steel needles, friend, and the fires will fight to host you. The dunes are hard on thread.
A quiet trade crosses the lines, yes. Everyone denies it. Everyone drinks the same smuggled tea. Politics is wonderful.

negative: Omens? Here's one: strangers who ask many questions have short winters.
The sky is grey, like always. Read your own fortune elsewhere.
neutral: Red sky means weather. Quiet birds mean weather. Out here everything means weather, and weather means digging.
Soldiers keep charms, sure. A button, a coin, a sister's ribbon. The charm works until it doesn't. Like armor.
positive: The cook swears three crows on the mess tent means an inspection, friend. Right twice now. We fear crows.
Bad omens we ignore; the quota arrives regardless. Good omens we drink to. It averages out to soup.

negative: Superstition is not intelligence. Neither is this conversation.
Omens are unverified data. So are you.
neutral: The red sky correlates with a wind shift, nothing more. We log weather, not prophecy.
Sentries reporting identical nightmares get a rest rotation, not an exorcism. Fatigue writes strange reports.
positive: Officially there are no omens, friend. Unofficially, nobody schedules an offensive on a fog moon. Nobody.
The signals crew keeps a lucky kettle. It has outlived three towers. Its service record is hard to argue with.

negative: The signs are speaking, yes. About you. We are still translating.
When the birds go silent, something is walking. This time it was you.
neutral: A ringed moon means wind from the deep desert in three days. Call it omen or forecast; pack your tent either way.
The land does know when battle comes. The beetles cross the road east. They have crossed east all week.
positive: For you, friend: when dawn is green at the rim, stay off the flats. Old wisdom, no explanation, never yet wrong.
Storms follow our war parties, they say. Sometimes. Sometimes we follow the storm. It is an old partnership.

negative: What moves at night? Patrols, wolves, and people we no longer discuss. Pick your category soon.
Night questions from a stranger. The dark here is spoken for.
neutral: After dark it's ration runners and wire menders, mostly. The heroic secret of night war: maintenance.
Dawn attacks are real. Dawn is when sentries dream of breakfast. Every army knows it; every army does it anyway.
positive: The digging sounds at night, friend? Sappers, ours or theirs, arguing underground in shovel language. Almost music.
The valley lights were ours — a wager over who could relay a lantern signal fastest. The loser is peeling roots.

negative: Night movement inquiries are a red flag stacked on your other red flags.
After-dark operations are not a topic. Your presence after dark is becoming one.
neutral: Night belongs to whoever has better discipline. We rotate double watches and hold our sectors till dawn.
Those ridge flashes are signal traffic. Encoded, so enjoy the pretty colors and nothing else.
positive: Watch the tower lights sometime, friend: three slow pulses means all quiet. Oddly comforting once you can read it.
Crossing between lines in the dark is possible. Surviving both sets of sentries is the advanced course. Not recommended.

negative: The night is our house. You are describing noises in our house.
Who moves in the dark? Tonight, mostly us, and one loud visitor. Hello.
neutral: The howl past midnight is wind through the bone-hollows. Mostly wind. The hollows earned their name honestly.
Campfires multiplying means one army wants to look bigger. Count the fires without cooks. Those are theater.
positive: The truth of night crossings, friend: follow the cold air, it pools along the safe low ground. The dead learned the hot paths.
Yes, we vanish at night. Into blankets, mostly. Even shadows must sleep. Keep that quiet — reputations feed families.

negative: Who's winning? Not you, if the questions continue.
The score is kept in our ledger and you're a debit. That's your whole scoreboard.
neutral: Who's winning? Whoever buried fewer this month. Get me the burial lists and I'll do the sums.
Stalemate is a city word. Out here we call it holding, and holding is our export.
positive: Between us, friend: nobody is winning, and we're built for exactly that. The line's patience compounds like interest.
The war turned once — the winter of the long quota. Ask all three armies who won that winter; enjoy three silences.

negative: Strategic outlooks are not shared with liabilities.
The balance of the war is above your clearance and beneath your conduct.
neutral: Current assessment: contested equilibrium. Two sides trade mass, one trades shadows, nobody banks a decisive gain.
Betting on the outcome is against regulations. The odds pool in the signals tent is therefore hypothetical.
positive: Candid forecast, friend: attrition favors the diggers, terrain favors the dunes, time favors whoever wastes least. We waste least.
How will history tell it? Cleanly, if we write it. We keep the better records. That's half the battle for history.

negative: Who wins? The sand is ahead by several thousand years. You are not gaining on it.
You ask about victory while accumulating defeats here. Curious bookkeeping.
neutral: The heavy armies wrestle; the desert keeps score; the score is secret. That is the war in one breath.
No side can win, say the travelers. Half right. No side can win quickly. Slowness is a country, and we are its citizens.
positive: For your ears, friend: each season the two great camps stand closer to each other and further from us. Let them.
When it ends, the histories will disagree, the wells will remain, and whoever keeps the wells keeps the ending.

negative: What do we say about you? We say numbers. Yours grows in the wrong direction.
Your name comes up at the count, stranger. Never in the good column.
neutral: Your name gets mentioned. Tone varies by tent. Keep your boots clean and it may settle.
First impression of you? 'Another wanderer.' The line was half right so far.
positive: The tents speak well of you, friend. One story has you carrying our wounded. It grows a little each telling. Let it.
The other camps ask about you, actually. We shrug and undersell. Consider it a courtesy between friends.

negative: Your file is thick, unflattering, and current. That is the word on you.
A way back for your name? There's a process. It starts with stopping. You haven't.
neutral: Assessment on record: unaffiliated, unpredictable, watch-listed. Improve two of three and the road gets smoother.
Yes, you're observed on the roads. Everyone is. You slightly more.
positive: Your record reads well, friend: fair dealing, no incidents, two commendable mentions. Yes, we track commendable.
Word moves between our posts faster than you walk. Lately the word on you is good. Sentries argue less when you approach.

negative: The fires say your name with a hiss lately. Fires are honest.
What do we call you? The polite version: 'the debt that walks.'
neutral: The wind carries your name occasionally. It has not yet decided what it thinks.
Stories about you? A few. Wild? Mild. Give the fires something better or something quieter.
positive: By the fires you are called 'the one who shares the road', friend. Such names are wells — deep, and hard to poison.
The children ask if you will visit again. That is the whole report, and better than any medal we could forge you.

negative: Fishwives, is it. The last man who mocked the line's talk now assists with laundry. Permanently.
Careful. Gossip is the one ration we never run short of. Neither are shovels.
neutral: Rumors are half true, like rations are half food. You learn to chew both.
Mock the gossip, miss the warning inside it. Your funeral. Literally, sometimes.
positive: Ha! True enough, friend. But our fishwives called last month's raid to the hour, so respect the net.
Laugh, but the rumor pot fed you today. You are drinking gossip soup right now.

negative: Dismiss our reporting again and you can test its accuracy from the wrong side of the wire.
That contempt is logged next to the intelligence you'll wish you'd had.
neutral: Rumor is unprocessed signal. We filter. You'd be surprised what survives filtering.
Some of it is noise. The rest saved lives twice this season. We tolerate the noise.
positive: Fair hit, friend. Even so, our 'gossip' has a source-grading system. The fishwives here hold clearances.
Mock away — but when you want the road report that's actually true, you'll queue like everyone else.

negative: The idle talk you mock has buried quicker tongues than yours.
We gossip like the wind gossips. Look what the wind does to mountains.
neutral: In the desert, rumor is water: some brackish, some sweet, all of it carried carefully.
True or not, a story that keeps a traveler off the wrong dune is truer than facts.
positive: Ha — yes, we are terrible gossips, friend. It is the desert's oldest entertainment. Stay; be gossiped about fondly.
Half of it is invention. Guess which half correctly, though, and you will live to be old and interesting.

negative: Leaving is your best rumor yet. Confirm it.
Go spread word somewhere the wire isn't watching you.
neutral: Off with you. If you hear anything about the eastern road, it's worth soup.
Gossip closes with the kitchen. Both reopen at dawn.
positive: Walk safe, friend. Bring back a rumor worth the stove seat.
Go on. We'll save your seat and the worst of the news.

negative: Exchange concluded. Your departure will be corroborated.
Go. The rumor mill logs its visitors too.
neutral: Copy. If you pass the south tower, tell them their relief is late.
Acknowledged. Treat everything you heard as unconfirmed. We do.
positive: Safe travels, friend. First rumor's free next time; bring one to trade after that.
Copy that. If the road tells you anything worth logging, our gate hears fairly.

negative: Take your questions to the horizon. It is patient with strangers.
Go. The fires will discuss you honestly in your absence.
neutral: May the news you carry stay lighter than your waterskin.
The road gossips too. Listen to it more than you talk.
positive: Go well, friend. The fire will keep a story warm for your return.
Travel softly. Bring us a rumor with sugar in it next time.
